title: Geometry-Aware Update Control for Robust Optimization

problem.claim: Training-time corruption can destabilize deep learning by causing abnormal optimization steps that drift, contaminate optimizer state, or permanently alter training trajectories.

contributions.claim: The work characterizes geometry-defined update perturbations involving directional deviation, orthogonal energy injection, heavy-tailed noise, and sign reversal.

The work introduces GAUC, an optimizer-side mechanism that evaluates updates using geometric consistency signals and selectively applies projection-based correction with scale-aware, budgeted clipping.
GAUC bounds the per-step influence of unreliable updates while preserving benign descent geometry, with optimizer and loss-function agnosticism, lightweight per-block state, and linear-time overhead.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that GAUC consistently stabilizes training under update-space perturbations.
The authors report that GAUC maintains performance under clean conditions.

narrative_sequence.summary: Training-time corruption is identified as a source of instability, with a small number of abnormal updates able to alter optimization trajectories.
The abstract locates these failures in update geometry and identifies several perturbation forms.
GAUC monitors incoming updates using recent descent history and constrains unreliable updates through geometric correction and clipping.
The authors report stabilization under update-space perturbations and maintained clean-condition performance.
